This invention concerns a disposable diaper designed to take in and retain discharged urine and feces. The diaper is configured with a front portion that contacts the wearer’s abdomen, a rear portion that contacts the wearer’s back, and a crotch portion where the front and rear portions continue lengthwise so as to extend between the wearer’s legs.

The disposable diaper comprises:

- a base layer having an absorbent body disposed toward an upper end in the longitudinal direction with respect to the center of the crotch portion, and first elastic members arranged along both longitudinal sides so that they surround the wearer’s legs;
- a cover layer placed above the absorbent body to cover the absorbent body; and
- a skin-contact layer arranged above the base layer to cover the cover layer.

The skin-contact layer includes an inlet cut portion formed by cutting it to a predetermined length, allowing urine and feces to move easily toward the cover layer or the absorbent body. The skin-contact layer also includes second elastic members positioned on both longitudinal sides, spaced from the inlet cut portion by predetermined distances, and configured to closely contact the wearer’s buttock skin along the lower layer side.
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a disposable diaper intended to absorb and receive bodily waste, particularly urine and feces, from a wearer. The diaper is configured to be worn comfortably on the body while securely containing excretions and reducing leakage during use.

The disposable diaper is generally divided into three main regions. These include a front surface part positioned on the front side of the wearer, a rear surface part positioned on the rear side of the wearer, and a gap part extending between the front surface part and the rear surface part. The gap part is arranged to pass between the wearer’s legs when the diaper is worn, thereby forming the crotch region of the diaper.

The diaper includes a base layer that forms a primary structural portion of the diaper. The base layer is provided with an absorber configured to absorb and retain urine and other liquid waste. In addition, first elastic members are arranged along both lengthwise side portions of the base layer. These first elastic members allow the diaper to closely fit around the wearer’s legs, helping to improve wearing comfort and prevent leakage through the leg openings.

A cover layer is positioned above the absorber. The cover layer covers the absorber and helps maintain the absorber in an appropriate position within the diaper. The cover layer may also assist in guiding liquid toward the absorber while preventing direct exposure of the absorber to the wearer’s skin.

A skin contact layer is further provided above the cover layer so as to cover the cover layer. This skin contact layer is the portion of the diaper that is positioned closest to the wearer’s skin during use. The skin contact layer includes an inlet cutting part through which urine and feces can pass into the interior of the diaper. The skin contact layer also includes second elastic members. These second elastic members help the skin contact layer maintain improved contact with the wearer’s buttocks, thereby enhancing fit, reducing gaps, and improving the ability of the diaper to receive and contain feces.

Through this layered structure, the disposable diaper provides effective absorption, improved fit around the legs and buttocks, and enhanced containment of urine and feces.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a disposable diaper designed to effectively receive, guide, and absorb urine and feces while maintaining a secure and comfortable fit on the wearer. The diaper is formed as a layered structure including a base layer, an absorbent member, a cover layer, and a skin contact layer. These layers cooperate to provide both liquid absorption and containment of solid or semi-solid waste, while also helping to prevent leakage during use.

The base layer forms the outer portion of the diaper and may be made of a liquid-impermeable or substantially liquid-impermeable sheet material so that absorbed fluids are prevented from escaping to the outside. Positioned on the inner side of the base layer is an absorber configured to receive and retain bodily excretions, particularly urine. The absorber may include absorbent fibers, superabsorbent polymer, or other suitable absorbent materials capable of rapidly taking in liquid and holding it even when pressure is applied.

A cover layer is arranged over the absorber to help distribute urine and other liquid excretions toward the absorbent member. Above this cover layer, on the side intended to face the wearer’s body, is a skin contact layer. The skin contact layer is positioned to lie close to the buttocks and surrounding skin during use. This layer improves fit and helps keep the diaper in close contact with the body, thereby reducing gaps through which waste could escape.

The skin contact layer includes a cut inlet or opening through which feces and other excretions can pass. This inlet is positioned in a region corresponding to the wearer’s anal area when the diaper is worn. As a result, feces can move through the opening and be delivered toward the underlying absorbent or receiving region, instead of spreading widely across the skin contact surface. This arrangement reduces smearing against the skin and improves containment within the diaper.

Elastic leg members are provided along the leg openings of the diaper. These elastic members gather the diaper around the wearer’s thighs and help create a close seal at the leg regions. In combination with the skin contact layer, the elastic leg members maintain the diaper in a stable position and improve the fit around the buttocks and crotch. This close contact helps direct bodily waste toward the intended inlet and absorber, while reducing the likelihood of side leakage.

In use, the diaper is worn so that the skin contact layer faces the wearer’s skin and the cut inlet is aligned with the area from which feces are discharged. Urine passing through the skin-facing layers is guided into the absorber, where it is retained. Feces pass through the cut inlet and are contained within the diaper structure, reducing contact with the skin and limiting movement of waste toward the leg openings or waist edges.

The key advantage of the invention is that it improves the delivery of excretions to the absorber and receiving space while maintaining close contact between the diaper and the wearer’s buttocks. By combining a layered absorbent construction, a dedicated inlet for waste passage, and elasticized leg portions, the diaper provides enhanced containment, improved fit, and better leakage prevention. This structure also contributes to comfort and hygiene by reducing the spread of excretions over the skin and by keeping waste more securely confined within the diaper.

**The Power of “The”**

The word **“the”** may be small, but it is one of the most important words in the English language. It is called a definite article, and it helps us talk about specific people, places, things, or ideas. For example, when we say “a book,” we mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book that the listener or reader can identify.

“The” gives clarity and precision to communication. It helps connect sentences, guide meaning, and show that something is already known or has been mentioned before. In phrases like “the sun,” “the world,” or “the future,” the word points to something unique or meaningful.

Although it is short and often unnoticed, “the” appears everywhere in English. It supports the structure of sentences and makes language more natural. Without it, English would sound incomplete and less clear. This simple word proves that even the smallest parts of language can have a powerful role.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a Korean patent translation-style description in English for a disposable diaper that improves the movement of urine and feces to an absorber through a cut inlet in the top layer.
counterfactuals.output:
**Description**

**DISPOSABLE DIAPER HAVING CUT INLET FOR TRANSFERRING URINE AND FECES TO ABSORBER**

**Technical Field**

The present invention relates to a disposable diaper, and more particularly, to a disposable diaper in which an inlet is formed by cutting a predetermined portion of a top layer contacting a wearer’s skin, so that urine and feces discharged from the wearer can be rapidly moved into an absorber positioned below the top layer.

**Background Art**

In general, a disposable diaper includes a liquid-permeable top sheet, a liquid-impermeable back sheet, and an absorbent body interposed therebetween. The top sheet is arranged toward the skin of a wearer and allows urine to pass therethrough. The absorbent body absorbs and retains the urine.

However, when the top sheet is formed in a flat sheet shape, feces, particularly soft feces, may remain on the surface of the top sheet for a long time. In this case, the feces are brought into contact with the skin of the wearer, thereby causing skin trouble such as rash or irritation. Also, even in the case of urine, if the urine is not quickly transferred to the absorbent body, a wet feeling may be increased.

Accordingly, there is a demand for a disposable diaper capable of guiding urine and feces toward an absorber more efficiently and reducing the contact time between excrement and the skin.

**Disclosure of Invention**

The present invention has been made in order to solve the above-described problems, and an object of the present invention is to provide a disposable diaper capable of improving movement of urine and feces to an absorber by forming a cut inlet in a top layer.

Another object of the present invention is to provide a disposable diaper in which the cut inlet is opened by pressure or weight of excrement, thereby allowing the excrement to be introduced into an inner space of the diaper while suppressing reverse leakage.

**Constitution of Invention**

A disposable diaper according to one embodiment of the present invention includes a back layer, an absorber disposed on the back layer, and a top layer disposed on the absorber and facing a wearer’s skin.

The top layer is provided with at least one cut inlet. The cut inlet is formed by cutting a part of the top layer, and is positioned in a region corresponding to a urine discharge portion and/or a feces discharge portion of the wearer. Urine or feces discharged from the wearer is introduced through the cut inlet and is moved to the absorber located below the top layer.

The cut inlet may be formed as a slit, a cross-shaped cut, a linear cut, an arcuate cut, an H-shaped cut, or a plurality of discontinuous cuts. The cut inlet may normally maintain a substantially closed state, and may be opened when urine or feces is applied thereto. Therefore, the surface area of the top layer contacting the wearer can be maintained while allowing excrement to be transferred downward.

The absorber may include a pulp material, a super absorbent polymer, or a mixed absorbent material. The absorber may be formed to have a recessed portion or a receiving space corresponding to the cut inlet, so that feces introduced through the cut inlet can be accommodated therein. In addition, a diffusion layer or acquisition layer may be provided between the top layer and the absorber, thereby distributing urine transferred through the cut inlet to a wider area of the absorber.

The top layer may be made of a nonwoven fabric having softness and liquid permeability. Around the cut inlet, an edge portion may be treated by embossing, thermal bonding, ultrasonic bonding, or coating, so that tearing of the top layer is prevented and an opening shape of the inlet is maintained.

**Mode for Carrying Out the Invention**

Hereinafter, the disposable diaper according to the present invention will be described in more detail.

The disposable diaper includes a diaper main body having a front waist region, a rear waist region, and a crotch region positioned between the front waist region and the rear waist region. The absorber is disposed at least in the crotch region and extends toward the front waist region and the rear waist region.

The top layer is arranged on an upper surface of the absorber. A cut inlet is formed in the top layer at the crotch region. In the case of an infant diaper, the cut inlet may be positioned at a central portion of the crotch region or slightly rearward from the central portion, so that both urine and feces can be guided to the absorber. In the case of a diaper for adults, a plurality of cut inlets may be provided according to body shape and discharge position.

When the wearer urinates, urine passes through the top layer and also enters the cut inlet. Since the cut inlet provides a direct passage to the absorber, the urine is rapidly moved downward and absorbed by the absorber. Thus, the amount of urine remaining on the surface of the top layer is reduced.

When the wearer discharges feces, particularly loose feces, the feces press the cut inlet by its own weight. The cut portion of the top layer is deformed downward, and the cut inlet is opened. The feces are introduced through the opened cut inlet into a space between the top layer and the absorber or directly into a receiving portion of the absorber. Accordingly, the feces are less exposed on the surface of the top layer, and contact with the skin of the wearer is reduced.

The cut inlet may be formed in a manner that a flap portion is created. The flap portion is a part of the top layer surrounded by the cut line and connected to the remaining top layer at one side. When excrement is applied, the flap portion bends downward and functions as a guide member for guiding the excrement to the absorber. After the excrement is introduced, the flap portion may return toward the original position, thereby reducing reverse movement of the excrement.

In addition, the top layer may include a hydrophilic portion around the cut inlet. The hydrophilic portion promotes movement of urine toward the cut inlet. Alternatively, the top layer may include a hydrophobic portion at a region contacting the skin, so that rewet and spreading of feces on the surface are suppressed.

The disposable diaper may further include side leakage prevention walls provided at both lateral sides of the top layer. The side leakage prevention walls prevent urine or feces introduced toward the cut inlet from leaking laterally. Elastic members may be provided in the side leakage prevention walls, leg portions, and waist portions.

**Effect of Invention**

According to the disposable diaper of the present invention, since the cut inlet is formed in the top layer, urine and feces can be rapidly moved to the absorber.

Further, since feces can be introduced into the inside of the diaper through the cut inlet, the amount of feces remaining on the skin-contacting surface is reduced, thereby decreasing skin irritation and improving wearing comfort.

Further, since the cut inlet can be opened only when excrement is applied and can otherwise remain substantially closed, reverse leakage of absorbed liquid or feces can be suppressed.

Further, the structure can be manufactured easily by cutting a predetermined portion of the top layer, and therefore productivity is excellent and manufacturing cost is not greatly increased.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for a disposable diaper divided into front, rear, and between-the-legs sections, including a base layer with an absorber, a cover layer, and a skin-contact layer with elastic members spaced from an inlet cut.
counterfactuals.output:
A disposable diaper can be configured as a body-fitting absorbent article divided, in its longitudinal direction, into a front section, a rear section, and a between-the-legs or crotch section located between the front and rear sections.

The diaper includes:

- **A base layer** extending across the front, crotch, and rear sections.  
  The base layer carries or incorporates an **absorbent body** for receiving and retaining urine or other bodily fluids.

- **A cover layer** arranged on the wearer-facing side of the base layer.  
  This cover layer helps cover the absorbent body and may guide discharged fluid toward the absorber while helping maintain the diaper’s shape.

- **A skin-contact layer** positioned above the cover layer so that it faces and contacts the wearer’s skin during use.  
  The skin-contact layer includes an **inlet cut** or opening through which bodily waste can pass toward the absorbent region below.

The skin-contact layer is provided with **elastic members** extending generally in the longitudinal direction of the diaper. These elastic members are arranged on opposite sides of the inlet cut, but are **spaced outwardly from the edge of the inlet cut** rather than being placed immediately adjacent to it. This spacing allows the region around the inlet cut to remain relatively soft and non-constricting against the wearer while the elastic members raise or shape the skin-contact layer to improve fit and help form a pocket-like space for receiving waste.

In use, the front and rear sections secure the diaper around the wearer’s waist, while the crotch section lies between the legs. The inlet cut in the skin-contact layer is positioned to receive excretion, and the absorbent body in the base layer absorbs liquid passing through the opening. The spaced elastic members improve body conformity, reduce leakage, and help prevent the edges of the inlet cut from pressing tightly or uncomfortably against the wearer’s skin.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
